## Purpose

Happens to have some 5090 cluster , so try to  contribute some MoE config profiling result.




1. **Qwen3-30B-A3B** with EP 8 and EP 4:
`E=32,N=768,device_name=NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_5090.json` for EP4
`E=16,N=768,device_name=NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_5090.json` for EP8

```
export VLLM_MOE_TUNE_CACHE_CLEAR_INTERVAL=0;
python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model  /mnt/nfs/model/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct/  --tp-size 4  --enable-expert-parallel  --tune 
```




2. **Mixtral 8x7b** with TP8 & TP4:

`E=8,N=3584,device_name=NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_5090.json` TP4

from

```
python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py --model  /mnt/nfs/model/Mistral/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1/  --tp-size 8  --tune
```


--------Below TP8  configs  have been removed ,asked by Gemini-AI --------------------
3. **DeepSeek-R1** with TP8     (although it's not quite practical to run 8x5090 for DeeepSeek-R1 )

`E=256,N=256,device_name=NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_5090,block_shape=[128,128].json` from

`E=128,N=96,device_name=NVIDIA_GeForce_RTX_5090.json ` for TP8

This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it has not had any activity within 90 days. It will be automatically closed if no further activity occurs within 30 days. Leave a comment if you feel this pull request should remain open. Thank you!

## Code Review

This pull request introduces several Triton configuration files for the fused_moe layer optimized for the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090. The review feedback identifies significant issues regarding the compatibility and optimality of these configurations. Specifically, several files appear to have been tuned for Tensor Parallelism (TP) rather than the default Expert Parallelism (EP) used in vLLM, which will prevent the runtime from correctly loading them. Furthermore, technical inconsistencies were found where BLOCK_SIZE_K values exceed the quantization block size, suggesting that the tuning parameters may be sub-optimal for the intended FP8 block-quantized kernels.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `BLOCK_SIZE_K` value (256) exceeds the quantization block size `group_k` (128) specified in the filename. For block-quantized MoE kernels, `BLOCK_SIZE_K` must be less than or equal to `group_k` (and ideally a divisor of it) to ensure that each Triton tile uses a single set of quantization scales. While the vLLM runtime currently caps `BLOCK_SIZE_K` at `min(block_n, block_k)`, having a config that specifies a larger value indicates that the tuning was likely performed on a non-block-quantized path (e.g., BF16), making the resulting parameters (`num_warps`, `num_stages`) sub-optimal for the actual FP8 block-quantized kernel. This issue affects multiple entries in this file (e.g., batch sizes 1, 2, 4, 16, 24, 96, 128).

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

This configuration for DeepSeek-R1 appears to have been tuned for Tensor Parallelism (TP) rather than Expert Parallelism (EP), as evidenced by the filename `E=256,N=256`. In vLLM, DeepSeek-V3/R1 models use EP by default. For a TP8 (EP) deployment, vLLM expects a configuration with `E=32` (local experts) and `N=2048` (intermediate size). Consequently, this file will not be automatically loaded during standard model execution. It is recommended to re-tune using the `--enable-expert-parallel` flag in the benchmark script to generate configs that match vLLM's runtime lookup logic for these models.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Similar to the DeepSeek config, this Qwen3-30B-A3B configuration seems tuned for TP4 (`E=128, N=192`) instead of the default EP4 (`E=32, N=768`). This file will likely be ignored by vLLM's config loader during standard inference because the expert count and intermediate size per rank do not match the EP sharding logic. Please consider re-tuning with `--enable-expert-parallel` to ensure the configs are correctly mapped and utilized.

inline_comments.body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The `BLOCK_SIZE_K` value (256) exceeds the quantization block size `group_k` (128) specified in the filename. For block-quantized MoE kernels, `BLOCK_SIZE_K` must be less than or equal to `group_k` (and ideally a divisor of it) to ensure that each Triton tile uses a single set of quantization scales. While the vLLM runtime currently caps `BLOCK_SIZE_K` at `min(block_n, block_k)`, having a config that specifies a larger value indicates that the tuning was likely performed on a non-block-quantized path (e.g., BF16), making the resulting parameters (`num_warps`, `num_stages`) sub-optimal for the actual FP8 block-quantized kernel. This issue affects multiple entries in this file (e.g., batch sizes 1, 2, 4, 16, 24, 96, 128).

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

This configuration for DeepSeek-R1 appears to have been tuned for Tensor Parallelism (TP) rather than Expert Parallelism (EP), as evidenced by the filename `E=256,N=256`. In vLLM, DeepSeek-V3/R1 models use EP by default. For a TP8 (EP) deployment, vLLM expects a configuration with `E=32` (local experts) and `N=2048` (intermediate size). Consequently, this file will not be automatically loaded during standard model execution. It is recommended to re-tune using the `--enable-expert-parallel` flag in the benchmark script to generate configs that match vLLM's runtime lookup logic for these models.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Similar to the DeepSeek config, this Qwen3-30B-A3B configuration seems tuned for TP4 (`E=128, N=192`) instead of the default EP4 (`E=32, N=768`). This file will likely be ignored by vLLM's config loader during standard inference because the expert count and intermediate size per rank do not match the EP sharding logic. Please consider re-tuning with `--enable-expert-parallel` to ensure the configs are correctly mapped and utilized.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces several Triton configuration files for the fused_moe layer optimized for the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090. The review feedback identifies significant issues regarding the compatibility and optimality of these configurations. Specifically, several files appear to have been tuned for Tensor Parallelism (TP) rather than the default Expert Parallelism (EP) used in vLLM, which will prevent the runtime from correctly loading them. Furthermore, technical inconsistencies were found where BLOCK_SIZE_K values exceed the quantization block size, suggesting that the tuning parameters may be sub-optimal for the intended FP8 block-quantized kernels.
